courses.title: Biology and Society
courses.description: [GE 5B] Fundamental concepts in biology are taught using socially relevant themes. Biological concepts are related to the major themes of evolution; structure and function; information flow, exchange and storage; transformations of energy and matter; and systems. Uses the study of biology to illustrate science as a way of knowing, the methods and practices of science, limits of scientific endeavors, ethics associated with biological investigations, and how biology can help inform decisions we make as individuals and as a society.

courses.title: Biology and Society Laboratory
courses.description: [GE 5C] A laboratory support course applying lecture concepts through hands-on, inquiry-based, learn-by-doing approaches. Supports students in majors that require fundamental concepts of biology as they relate to the major themes of evolution; structure and function; information flow exchange and storage; transformations of energy and matter; and systems. Uses the study of biology to illustrate science as a way of knowing, the methods and practices of science, limits of scientific endeavors, ethics associated with biological investigation, and how biology can help inform decisions we make as individuals and as a society. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1110 or BIO 1150 ; BIO 1150 can be concurrent. Pre or Corequisite(s):

courses.title: Foundations of Biology: Evolution, Ecology, and Biodiversity
courses.description: Using the central lens of evolution, this course will examine the reproduction, development, interactions, and adaptations of organisms within their environments. Bacteria, plants, animals, and all other lineages of life, at all levels of biological organization, will be explored. Corequisite(s): BIO 1220L .

courses.title: Foundations of Biology: Evolution, Ecology, and Biodiversity Laboratory
courses.description: Using hands-on activities, including field surveys and dissections, students will examine the diversity of life. Evolutionary and ecological perspectives to life’s biodiversity will be emphasized, as will the application of the practices of science. Corequisite(s): BIO 1220 .

courses.title: Form and Function in Plants
courses.description: The interplay between the anatomy and morphology of green plants and their physiology. The anatomical and physiological bases of development, growth regulation, water relations, reproduction, and the production and transport of food. Corequisite(s): BIO 2050L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L , or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Form and Function in Plants Laboratory
courses.description: Investigations of the anatomy, morphology, physiology, reproduction, and phylogeny of green plants. Emphasis is place on the exploration of the function and arrangement of tissues in organs, the major photosynthetic strategies, the effects of the environment on plant water relations, and the relationship between life cycles and the green plant phylogeny. Corequisite(s): BIO 2050 .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L , or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Plant Physiology
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 12-18 units
courses.description: An overview of physiological processes in plants including water relations, soils, mineral nutrition, photosynthesis, and responses to environmental (biotic and abiotic) influences on plant growth. In depth examination of how environmental signals are processed via hormones in controlling gene expression and plant development. Corequisite(s): BIO 4480L .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201/BOT 201L, or BIO 2050 / BIO 2050L .

courses.title: Plant Physiology Laboratory
courses.description: Inquiry-based laboratory exercises involving plant water relations, enzyme isolation and analysis, aseptic culture of plant material, mineral deficiencies, enzyme activity in germination and later development of tissues, as well as photoperiodism and hormonal influences on plant growth and development. Corequisite(s): BIO 4480 .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201/BOT 201L, or BIO 2050 / BIO 2050L .

courses.title: Marine Botany
courses.description: Evolution, development, reproduction, morphology, taxonomy, physiology, and ecology of marine algae. A focus is placed on the identification and study of local species. Corequisite(s): BIO 4490L .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201/BOT 201L, or BIO 2050 / BIO 2050L .

courses.title: Marine Botany Laboratory
courses.description: Field and laboratory investigations of marine algae. A focus is placed on the identification and study of local species, including experiences in experimental design, field research, data analyses, and scientific writing. Weekend field trips are required. Weekend field trips are required. Weekend field trips are required. Corequisite(s): BIO 4490 .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201/BOT 201L, or BIO 2050 / BIO 2050L .

courses.title: California Flora
courses.description: Introduction to the plant communities of California and their dominant species, with special attention given to those in the California Floristic Province. Botanical terminology used in dichotomous keys and identification books and online resources will be explained, along with descriptions of the major plant families of California in terms of their vegetative and floral characteristics. Corequisite(s): BIO 4500L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L ; or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: California Flora Laboratory
courses.description: Identification of California wild land plants using dichotomous keys and other resources. Recognition of common plant families. Overview of the geographic distribution of plants in southern California. Corequisite(s): BIO 4500 .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L ; or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Evolution of Plants
courses.description: Evolution of plants as illustrated by the comparative morphology, life cycles and other reproductive patterns, molecular characteristics, and fossil record of green algae and land plants. Corequisite(s): BIO 4520L .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201/BOT 201L and BIO 413; or BIO 2050 / BIO 2050L and BIO 3240 .

courses.title: Evolution of Plants Laboratory
courses.description: The evolution of plants will be investigated through the comparative morphology, life cycles, and other reproductive patterns of the green plants. Methods will include observations of fossils, live, and preserved specimens. Corequisite(s): BIO 4520 .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201/BOT 201L and BIO 413; or BIO 2050 / BIO 2050L and BIO 3240 .

courses.title: Plant Anatomy
courses.description: Origin, development, and characteristics of cells, tissues, and tissue systems in the roots, stems, and leaves of vascular plants. Corequisite(s): BIO 4530L .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201/BOT 201L or BIO 2050 / BIO 2050L .

courses.title: Plant Anatomy Laboratory
courses.description: Microscopic study of representative plants concerning the origin, development, and characteristics of cells, tissues, and tissue systems in the roots, stems, and leaves of vascular plants. Corequisite(s): BIO 4530 .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201/BOT 201L or BIO 2050 / BIO 2050L .

courses.title: Plant Genetics
courses.description: Principles and processes in classical and modern plant genetics. Topics include Mendelian genetics, gene regulation, genome architecture and evolution, and plant genomics.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 121/BIO 121L, BIO 122/BIO 122L, and BIO 123/BIO 123L; BIO 121/BIO 121L and BIO 122/BIO122L/BIO 1220C; BIO 121/BIO 121L/BIO 1210B and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L ; or BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L . BIO 2400 and BIO 2050 recommended.

courses.title: Plant Development and Differentiation
courses.description: The role of external and internal cues such as hormones, temperature, signaling in germination, growth and reproduction of plants. Advanced topics such floral biology including pollination and floral development will also be covered.
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201/BOT 201L, or BIO 2050 / BIO 2050L .

courses.title: Plants and the Environment
courses.description: Study of the interrelationships between plants and their environment with an emphasis on the response of plant species, populations, communities, and ecosystems to changing abiotic and biotic conditions. Corequisite(s): BIO 4570L .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201, BOT 201L, BIO 211L, BIO 325 and BIO 325L; or BIO 2050 , BIO 2050L , BIO 2110L , BIO 3250W and BIO 3250LW .

courses.title: Plants and the Environment Laboratory
courses.description: Application of field and laboratory techniques used by plant ecologists to study physiology, populations, communities, and ecosystems. Corequisite(s): BIO 4570 .
courses.prerequisites: BOT 201/201L BIO 211L and BIO 325/325L, or BIO 2050 / BIO 2050L , BIO 2110L and BIO 3250W / BIO 3250LW .

courses.title: Entomology
courses.description: Insect structure and function, evolution, growth and development, behavior, ecology, and influence on human societies; includes a survey of the major insect groups.
courses.prerequisites: Junior standing and any 2000 level BIO course.

courses.title: Entomology Laboratory
courses.description: Primary focus is on the identification/ classification and natural history of common Insect Orders and Families. A group field project that involves insect sampling and quantitative analysis of samples is required. The field project may be used to satisfy the departmental capstone requirement.
courses.prerequisites: Junior standing and any 2000 level BIO course.

courses.title: Genetics
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 0-6 units
courses.description: The flow of genetic information involving DNA, RNA and protein. Introduction to patterns of inheritance, transmission (Mendelian) genetics, nuclear structure, mechanisms of gene expression, genomics, molecular genetics and recombinant DNA technology.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L , or BIO 1150 / BIO 1150L .

courses.title: Principles of Evolution
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 0-6 units
courses.description: A study of biological evolution as a natural process resulting in the generation of biodiversity and ultimately the origin of humans. Overview of the basic principles of scientific knowledge and the history of evolutionary thinking, leading to the development of the modern Theory of Evolution. Review of the origin and history of life on Earth and the fossil record. Analysis of evolutionary processes at the molecular, organismal, and ecosystem levels.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 123/BIO 123L and BIO 303; or BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L and BIO 2400 ; or BIO 122/BIO 122L and BIO 1220C.

courses.title: Principles of Ecology
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 0-6 units
courses.description: Survey of ecological theory and practice, including interactions between organisms and their abiotic and biotic environment. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L , BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L , and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Interpretation of Science Service Learning
courses.description: Methods and techniques necessary to develop professional oral interpretive skills in the sciences. Students will design and develop formal interpretive nature walks that enhance their audience’s understanding and appreciation of science and nature. Corequisite(s): BIO 4910AS .
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing; BIO 121/BIO 121L, BIO 122/BIO 122L, and BIO 123/BIO 123L; BIO 121/BIO 121L and BIO 122/BIO122L/BIO 1220C; BIO 121/BIO 121L/BIO 1210B and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L ; or BIO 1210 / BIO 1210L and BIO 1220 / BIO 1220L .

courses.title: Elements of Organic Chemistry
courses.description: The fundamental concepts of organic chemistry will be presented, for students who are required to take one semester of organic chemistry. Topics covered include chemical bonding, molecular structure, stereochemistry, nomenclature, physical properties, thermodynamics and kinetics, acid-base chemistry, organic reaction mechanisms, synthesis and biomolecules. Not open to chemistry majors. Not open to chemistry majors.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 123 or CHM 1220 ; and CHM 123L or CHM 1220L .

courses.title: Elements of Organic Chemistry Laboratory
courses.description: Introduction to general techniques of the organic laboratory for the separation, purification and identification of organic substances. Survey of simple reactions of various functional groups. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: CHM 123 or CHM 1220 ; and CHM 123L or CHM 1220L ; or concurrent enrollment in CHM 2010 .

courses.title: Organic Chemistry I
courses.description: Modern concepts of chemical bonding, molecular structure, conformations, nomenclature, thermodynamics and kinetics, acid-base chemistry, stereochemistry, organic reaction intermediates and mechanisms, and synthesis. The physical properties, preparations and reactions of alkanes, haloalkanes, alkenes, alkynes and alcohols.
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in CHM 123 or CHM 1220 ; and C- or better in CHM 123L or CHM 1220L .
